# A nonconstant PSD test directed at one prescribed central chord

## 1. Actual geometry and indices

Use the canonical six rays with actual endpoint radii

    P_0=(A,0), P_1=(0,B), P_2=(-t,t),
    P_3=(-a,0), P_4=(0,-b), P_5=(r,-r),

where all six letters are positive. Let W_i be the actual area between P_i and P_(i+1), cyclically. Thus

    (W_0,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4,W_5)
      =(Y_3,X_2,Y_1,X_3,Y_2,X_1),

where X_i is the area in precisely cap i, and Y_i the area in the other two caps. The actual cap areas and total are

    q_1=W_0+W_4+W_5,
    q_2=W_0+W_1+W_2,
    q_3=W_2+W_3+W_4,
    k=sum_i W_i.

The three normalized chord lengths are B+b, A+a, r+t. If B+b is the largest, its normalized inverse weight is

    lambda_1=(1/(B+b))/[1/(B+b)+1/(A+a)+1/(r+t)].

This note derives an exact simultaneous-area test directed at the two endpoints P_1,P_4 of that chord. It does not prove the desired lower bound for lambda_1.

## 2. The exact six-cycle matrix in these coordinates

Let

    (R_0,...,R_5)=(A,B,t,a,b,r).

Consecutive and next-neighbor determinants are respectively R_i R_(i+1) and R_(i-1)R_(i+1). The exact sector PSD criterion therefore becomes the cyclic matrix with

    h_i=1/(R_i R_(i+1))-1/(2W_i)>=0,
    ell_i=1/(2W_(i-1))+1/(2W_i)-1/R_i^2,
    L_ii=ell_i, L_(i,i+1)=-h_i.                 (1)

The core-area conditions W_i>=R_i R_(i+1)/2 are part of these data. The matrix must be positive semidefinite for every actual convex body with those endpoints and areas, and conversely that condition constructs an actual polygon.

The formula for ell_i follows by cancellation in b_i-h_(i-1)-h_i; in particular it includes the full radial geometry. No independent envelope area has been substituted.

## 3. Exact elimination of the two intervening paths

Define the determinants of the two disjoint path blocks by

    Delta_23=ell_2 ell_3-h_2^2,
    Delta_05=ell_0 ell_5-h_5^2.                  (2)

Assume first that both path blocks are positive definite. This holds, for example, when all h_i are positive and L is PSD: a singular proper path block would have a nonzero null vector whose extension by zero has zero full quadratic form; for a PSD matrix that extension is in the full kernel, and the positive edges from the path to its omitted endpoints force the path vector to vanish. The two-node statement also follows directly from its equations. More generally the explicit positive-definiteness hypothesis is sufficient below.

Fix endpoint values x_1=z and x_4=w. The minimizing values on the two paths are

    x_2=(ell_3 h_1 z+h_2 h_3 w)/Delta_23,
    x_3=(h_2 h_1 z+ell_2 h_3 w)/Delta_23,
    x_0=(ell_5 h_0 z+h_5 h_4 w)/Delta_05,
    x_5=(h_5 h_0 z+ell_0 h_4 w)/Delta_05.         (3)

These follow by solving the two positive-definite two-by-two systems obtained by differentiating x^T L x. For z,w>=0 all four values are nonnegative, because the diagonal entries of a positive-definite path block are positive and h_i>=0.

Substitution, or completing the two squares, gives the exact minimum

    min x^T L x = alpha z^2-2 gamma z w+delta w^2,               (4)

where

    alpha=ell_1-h_1^2 ell_3/Delta_23-h_0^2 ell_5/Delta_05,
    delta=ell_4-h_3^2 ell_2/Delta_23-h_4^2 ell_0/Delta_05,
    gamma=h_1 h_2 h_3/Delta_23+h_0 h_5 h_4/Delta_05.            (5)

Consequently, under the positive-definite path-block hypothesis, exact sector feasibility is equivalent to

    alpha>=0, delta>=0, alpha delta>=gamma^2.                  (6)

Indeed the completed path-square terms are nonnegative, so (6) is equivalent to nonnegativity of the entire quadratic form. Conversely a violation of (6) supplies a negative test in (4). Since gamma>=0, one may choose the violating endpoint values z,w nonnegative; (3) then provides an explicit nonnegative, generally nonconstant, witness vector for the full matrix.

This is a two-endpoint test that retains both paths and all six actual sector areas. It is stronger than retaining a single endpoint's diagonal inequality or an independent unique-sector envelope.

## 4. Polynomial necessary conditions retaining degenerate cases

Put P=Delta_23 Delta_05 and define

    F=ell_1 P-h_1^2 ell_3 Delta_05-h_0^2 ell_5 Delta_23,
    G=ell_4 P-h_3^2 ell_2 Delta_05-h_4^2 ell_0 Delta_23,
    J=h_1 h_2 h_3 Delta_05+h_0 h_5 h_4 Delta_23.                (7)

Every actual feasible body satisfies

    Delta_23>=0, Delta_05>=0,
    F>=0, G>=0, FG>=J^2.                                     (8)

When both determinants are positive, these are exactly the cleared-denominator conditions in (6). When either is zero, their necessity follows by applying the preceding argument to L+epsilon I, epsilon>0, and then taking epsilon down to zero in the displayed finite polynomials. This is only a continuity argument for a fixed six-by-six matrix, not an approximation of bodies, fibers or selected centers.

At zero determinants, (8) alone need not be sufficient. The full PSD criterion, or the relevant range conditions in a singular Schur complement, must be retained. In particular isolated zero-eigenvalue path components cannot be inverted silently.

A concrete chord-weighted necessary test is obtained from z=B,w=b in (4). After clearing denominators it gives

    F B^2-2J B b+G b^2>=0.                                    (9)

It also remains necessary in degenerate cases by the same polynomial argument. Optimizing both endpoint values, as in (6), is stronger than this one chosen test.

## 5. An independent falsification screen and its exact limitation

The script `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/screen_exact_psd_ordinary_weight_slab_recovery.py` tests the unresolved ordinary implication using the exact simultaneous matrix (1), the actual core-area constraints, all three cap fractions <=128/279, and the sorted profile q_min+q_mid+q_max/4<=k. It normalizes k=1 and minimizes the first inverse weight after imposing B+b>=A+a,r+t.

One hundred numerical starts found no value below 2/9. The best numerical candidates are near 0.232289, with several matrix eigenvalues near zero; their residuals are floating-point quantities, not exact feasibility certificates. The saved output `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/exact_psd_ordinary_weight_slab_recovery_best.json` is therefore only a falsification/search record. It is not a verified minimizer, a lower-bound proof, a certified polygon, or evidence of a symmetry reduction.

Equations (1)–(9) are proved exact statements independent of this computation. The ordinary implication itself remains unresolved in this note.
